sentences.text:
The claimants in M.V.C. No.277/2018 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Shorapur [hereinafter referred to as 'the tribunal' for brevity]
are before this Court challenging the judgment and award dated 04.09.2019 passed therein by which their claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act was dismissed.
2. Briefly stated the facts are, that appellant No.1 is the wife, appellant Nos.2 and 3 are the daughter and son and appellant No.4 is the mother of deceased Khasimsab, who was working as a driver-cum-conductor at the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation, Bengaluru.

On 10.05.2017 when he was riding a motorcycle from Shorapur to Bachimatti NC: 2026:KHC-K:8-DB HC-KAR Village, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-48/H- 7792 ridden from opposite side dashed against it.
As a result of the accident, Mr.Khasimsab suffered injuries and later succumbed.

A claim petition was filed by the appellants claiming compensation of Rs.91,50,000/-
along with interest from the owner and insurer of the offending motorcycle.
3. The respondents in the claim petition were served and represented.
The respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle filed a counter denying the accident as well as the injuries and the negligence attributed to the rider of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle also filed a statement denying the assertions made in the claim petition.

The owner of the motorcycle on which the deceased was riding also filed a counter stating that the vehicle was duly insured and that the rider of the motorcycle had a valid license and therefore it is respondent No.2 which is liable to indemnify the appellants.

The respondent No.4 being the insurer of the vehicle which was ridden by the deceased denied the assertions made in the claim petition and also alleged that the rider of the offending motorcycle was negligent and was responsible for the accident.

sentences.text: Based on these contentions, the Tribunal held a trial where at appellant No.1 was examined as PW-1 and she marked Exhibits P-1 to P-9.

The respondents were examined as RW-1 to 3 and they marked Exhibits R-1 to R-7.
4.

The tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased and that the appellants had failed to adduce sufficient evidence to prove that the accident was caused due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
Consequently, it proceeded to dismiss the claim petition.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellants are before this Court.

5. The learned counsel for the appellants contended that both the vehicles were involved in a head-on collision and that the owner of the offending vehicle had admitted that the police had filed a charge-sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle.
He therefore contends that the tribunal did not consider this material fact and erroneously held that the deceased was negligent and responsible for the accident.

He also contends that when both the vehicles were involved in a NC:
2026:KHC-K:8-DB HC-KAR head-on collision, the tribunal should have attributed negligence to both of them equally, in which event, the appellants was entitled to 50% of the compensation.

6. Per contra, the learned counsel for insurer of offending vehicle contends that the offending vehicle was covered by policy of insurance which was in force for the period 07.11.2014 to 06.11.2015, but the date of accident in question was on 10.05.2017.
He therefore contends that respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the appellants.
7. She also claimed that Exhibit R-3 which was marked by the owner of the offending vehicle is a fake policy.

She however contends that due to the reasons beyond the control of respondent No.4,
evidence was not adduced in that regard.
She therefore prays that the impugned judgment and award be set aside and the case be remitted for reconsideration.

8. Having regard to the fact that two vehicles were involved in the accident, the Tribunal must have applied the test declared by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prabhavathi and Others v.
Managing Director, NC: 2026:KHC-K:8-DB HC-KAR Bangalore Metropolitan, Transport Corporation - 2025 SCC OnLine 455.

entities.text:
Prabhavathi and Others v.
Managing Director, NC: 2026:KHC-K:8-DB HC-KAR Bangalore Metropolitan, Transport Corporation - 2025 SCC OnLine 455
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It also must have taken into account the overall evidence that was adduced before it to ascertain the probability of the involvement of both the vehicles in the causation of the accident.
The policy of insurance produced and marked as Exhibit R-3 indicates that the offending vehicle was covered by a policy of insurance.
However, since it is stated by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that the said policy of insurance was fake, it also must have adduced enough evidence to establish the same.
Therefore, we are of the view that the tribunal must have been circumspect in considering the case of the appellants from a proper perspective.
Consequently, the impugned judgment and award dated 04.09.2019 passed in MVC No.277/2018 by the Senior Civil judge and MACT, Shorapur warranted interference.
9. Accordingly, appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal in MVC No.277/2018 is set aside.
The matter is remitted back to the tribunal for reconsideration.

It is open for the appellants as well as the respondents to adduce any further evidence, if they are NC:
